sections.title: 📖 What is Prosody?
sections.content: Prosody (Chandas) is the study of poetic meters. Sanskrit poetry has beautiful metrical patterns that make it musical and memorable.

key_concepts.definition: A syllable with a long vowel or ending in a consonant
A syllable with a short vowel not followed by a consonant

common_meters.name: Anushtubh (अनुष्टुभ्)
common_meters.description: The most common meter in classical Sanskrit. Used in the Ramayana and Mahabharata.
common_meters.example: रामो राजमणिः सदा। (Rama is always the jewel of kings.)

common_meters.name: Indravajra (इन्द्रवज्रा)
common_meters.description: A meter with 11 syllables per line.

common_meters.name: Upendravajra (उपेन्द्रवज्रा)
common_meters.description: A variation of Indravajra with 11 syllables.

common_meters.name: Vasantatilaka (वसन्ततिलका)
common_meters.description: A elegant meter with 14 syllables per line.

famous_examples.example1: वदनं कमलं समम्। (The face is like a lotus.)
famous_examples.example2: ज्ञानं सर्वार्थसाधनम्। (Knowledge is the means to all purposes.)

questions.question: What is the most common meter in classical Sanskrit?
questions.explanation: Anushtubh is the most common meter, used in the Ramayana and Mahabharata.

questions.question: What is a 'Guru' syllable?
questions.explanation: A 'Guru' (heavy) syllable has a long vowel or ends in a consonant.

questions.question: Which meter is known for being elegant with 14 syllables?
